input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: The second § 12.4 imposes a non-compete on Customer running during the term and for twenty-four months afterwards over any competing product or service in any territory. That is walk-away territory under NONCOMPETE (post-term restraint longer than 12 months, undefined scope) and fails every fallback element: no named product, post-term application, 24 months, and no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no non-compete commitment. The no-hire sentence in the first § 12.4 is a non-solicitation term and is not double-flagged here. We take the preferred position by striking the offending sentence outright; retained § 12.3 already confirms in operative terms that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service in any field or territory, so no replacement permission is needed.

ops.oldText: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a non-compete or field-of-use restriction on our business, so we have struck the prohibition in the second § 12.4; it also contradicted § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we made no non-compete commitment and which continues to confirm our freedom of action. If Vendor needs protection, we could discuss a restriction limited to a single named competing product, during the term only and capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Strike the two-year post-term non-compete on Customer in § 12.4

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
